evidenceMatrix.hypothesis: Local-timezone Date methods applied to a UTC ISO timestamp produce a different calendar date when the runtime timezone differs from the developer's timezone

environmentEvidence.summary: SHADOWBOX TZ = UTC - explicitly set in Dockerfile
2024-01-14T23:30:00Z resolves to Jan 15 in IST, Jan 14 in UTC
TZ is the sole differentiating factor between local and SHADOWBOX

codeEvidence.summary: isDueToday() uses d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate() - all local-TZ
Input declared as UTC ISO string; output derived in local timezone - contract mismatch
Exactly 3 TZ-sensitive tests fail; 2 TZ-independent tests pass - matches 2/3 split
Runtime verified: IST getDate()=15, UTC getDate()=14 for edge timestamp

ciEvidence.summary: SHADOWBOX Docker = UTC = standard CI default - failure confirmed by proxy
Any UTC Linux CI runner would produce identical 3-failure result
test:utc script confirms developer awareness that CI runs in UTC

reproductionEvidence.summary: Local: 5/5 pass (TZ=Asia/Calcutta, no TZ env var)
npm run test:utc: 2/5 pass, 3/5 fail (TZ=UTC, same code)
SHADOWBOX Docker: 5 total, 2 pass, 3 fail, exit code 1 - FAILURE REPRODUCED

evidenceMatrix.confidenceRationale: The mechanism is directly observable at runtime. The exact same code produces different outputs when TZ changes. All three investigator streams converge on the same finding with no contradicting evidence.

rootCauseCandidate.title: Timezone-implicit calendar date extraction from a UTC timestamp
rootCauseCandidate.summary: isDueToday() in demo-app/src/invoiceChecker.js constructs a local calendar date string from a UTC ISO timestamp using JavaScript's local-timezone Date methods (getFullYear, getMonth, getDate). When the server timezone (UTC) differs from the developer's timezone (IST, UTC+5:30), the derived calendar date for timestamps near midnight differs by one day, causing three tests to fail.
mechanismStepByStep: 1. Test passes timestamp '2024-01-14T23:30:00.000Z' and target date '2024-01-15' to isDueToday()
2. new Date('2024-01-14T23:30:00.000Z') creates a Date object representing a fixed instant in time
3. d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate() are called - these return LOCAL timezone components
4. In IST (UTC+5:30): the instant is 2024-01-15 05:00 IST => getDate() returns 15 => localDateStr = '2024-01-15' => matches targetDate => true
5. In UTC: the instant is 2024-01-14 23:30 UTC => getDate() returns 14 => localDateStr = '2024-01-14' => does not match '2024-01-15' => false
6. The test asserts === true, so it fails in UTC
7. getInvoicesDueOn() calls isDueToday() per invoice, so INV-001 is excluded in UTC, reducing the set from [INV-001, INV-002] to [INV-002] and the total from 1250 to 750
rootCauseCandidate.whyFailureOccurs: The local-timezone Date methods project a fixed UTC instant onto a local wall-clock calendar. When the UTC timestamp falls between 18:30 UTC and 23:59 UTC (the 5h30m window before IST midnight), IST returns the next calendar day while UTC returns the current calendar day. The test was written assuming IST semantics.
missingEvidenceToConfirm: Actual CI platform configuration (GitHub Actions workflow) to confirm CI also runs UTC - currently inferred from SHADOWBOX Docker proxy
Test run on a UTC+0 non-Docker environment (e.g. bare Linux server with TZ=UTC) to confirm the Docker layer itself is not a confounding factor - low probability but untested

fix.description: Replace d.getFullYear()/getMonth()/getDate() with d.getUTCFullYear()/getUTCMonth()/getUTCDate() in isDueToday(). This makes date extraction timezone-independent and consistent with the UTC ISO input contract.

confidenceJustification: All three independent investigators (Environment, Code, CI) identify the same root cause through different evidence paths. The failure is deterministically reproducible by changing a single environment variable. Runtime verification confirms the exact numeric difference (getDate()=15 vs 14). No contradicting evidence exists.
recommendedNextStep: Phase 4: Apply the fix (3 getDate->getUTCDate substitutions), run regression tests in both local and SHADOWBOX environments, confirm 5/5 pass in both, and commit the fix with the evidence trail.
